builder_plan.scenario: Start with one repeated product task that has a measurable failure or cost.
builder_plan.change: Read the methods and identify one change you can isolate in that workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current implementation on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful outcomes, response time, human rework, and total cost per successful task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: A Runtime System for Mitigating Crossbar Port Contention on SM-Partitioned GPUs
summary: GPCPlace replaces the default SM-spreading behavior of CUDA Green Contexts with a runtime that profiles workloads and dynamically chooses between spreading and packing SMs across GPCs, hooking CUDA driver kernel launches to set SM masks without application changes. It costs a per-GPU profiling pass and driver-level integration complexity, and adds a runtime dependency outside standard frameworks. It can fail because neither spreading nor packing is universally faster, gains are workload- and GPU-specific (average 1.15x, often less), and the benefit only materializes when multiple workloads genuinely share one GPU under crossbar port contention.
rationale: The technique targets CUDA kernel-level SM placement for co-located workloads rather than LLM serving, so its value for a small-team ML engineer depends entirely on whether they run concurrent latency-critical and background workloads on the same GPU.
technique: Dynamic GPC-aware SM partitioning for concurrent GPU workloads

claims.statement: GPCPlace replaces the default SM-spreading behavior of CUDA Green Contexts with a runtime that profiles workloads and dynamically chooses between spreading and packing SMs across GPCs, hooking CUDA driver kernel launches to set SM masks without application changes. It costs a per-GPU profiling pass and driver-level integration complexity, and adds a runtime dependency outside standard frameworks. It can fail because neither spreading nor packing is universally faster, gains are workload- and GPU-specific (average 1.15x, often less), and the benefit only materializes when multiple workloads genuinely share one GPU under crossbar port contention.
Speeds up latency-critical workloads by up to 1.15x on average and 2.38x maximum over CUDA Green Contexts, across 14 GPUs and 112 workload cases, without degrading throughput.
